message.content:
In ancient Greece, the establishment of laws and social order was carried out through a combination of formal institutions and notable law‑making figures:

| Institution / Person | Role in Lawmaking |
|-----------------------|-------------------|
| **Ekklesia (Assembly)** | The main democratic body where citizens voted on legislation. |
| **Boule (Council of 500)** | Selected by lot, it prepared proposals for the Assembly and oversaw daily governance. |
| **Archons** | Magistrates elected annually; some had judicial duties and could propose laws. |
| **Draco (c. 7th century BC)** | First known lawgiver of Athens; his code was famously harsh (“draconian”). |
| **Solon (c. 594 BC)** | Reformed Athenian law, reducing debt slavery and establishing legal equality. |
| **Cleisthenes (c. 508 BC)** | Implemented democratic reforms, reorganized the citizenry into demes, and set up new political structures. |
| **Lycurgus (c. 8th–7th century BC)** | Legendary Spartan lawgiver; instituted military‑oriented laws and strict social regulations. |

These lawmakers and institutions together shaped the legal framework and civic order of their respective city‑states.
